text:
olivia: FYI customer on Pro tier reports sudden 401s and repeated auth failures after switching to an editable install of the Python SDK with extras. They said it was working yesterday and the change was 'pip install -e .[auth]'.

olivia: Repro steps they gave (copied):
```
git clone git@github.com:acme/app.git
cd app/services/llm
pip install -e .[auth]
python main.py  # app starts but API calls fail with 401s
```

olivia: Their pyproject excerpt for extras:
```
[tool.poetry.extras]
auth = ["httpx>=0.23", "requests>=2.28"]
```

olivia: Sample runtime log from customer (sanitized):
```
INFO calling /v1/generate
ERROR 401 Unauthorized - Authorization: Bearer None
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "main.py", line 42, in <module>
    resp = client.generate(prompt)
  File "/workspace/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py", line 12, in generate
    return httpx.post(...)
AttributeError: module 'httpx' has no attribute 'post'
```

raj: hmm looks like two things: (1) Authorization header is missing (Bearer None) -> env var not loaded or client not reading token. (2) "httpx has no attribute post" usually means import shadowing (a folder named httpx or wrong version installed).

carla: +1 on shadowing. Editable installs commonly cause local package layout to hide deps. Can you ask for `python -c "import httpx; print(httpx.__file__, httpx.__version__)"` and `pip freeze`?

olivia: asked customer for those. They replied: `httpx` points to `/workspace/app/httpx/__init__.py` (ouch) and `httpx==0.15.0` in pip freeze. They also have a local package named `httpx` in their repo (legacy vendored copy).

mike: that explains AttributeError (old vendored httpx lacked API). The missing header might be because our SDK does something like `from httpx import AsyncClient as httpx` in some path and import resolution picks their package -> break client code that reads env vars in `__init__.py`.

raj: immediate mitigation: 1) ask customer to uninstall editable and install pinned wheel: `pip uninstall -y httpx && pip install .[auth] --no-build-isolation` or better `pip install dist/redwood_sdk-2.1.0-py3-none-any.whl` from our release. 2) Or rename their local `httpx` package (temporary).

olivia: customer tried `pip uninstall httpx` then `pip install httpx==0.23.3` and switched to non-editable install `pip install .` -> 401s went away, calls succeed. They reported app back to normal.

carla: long-term fix ideas: document editable-install caveat in troubleshooting guide; add check in our SDK on import to detect known broken httpx versions and emit a clear warning (and raise early). Also consider namespace protection for imports (use importlib.metadata to verify package origin).

raj: agree. I'll file an internal bug for a defensive import error message and a small code change: detect if imported httpx resolves from project path and raise a helpful error recommending reinstall.

mike: also add a short bullet in support playbook: if 401 + "AttributeError: module 'httpx' has no attribute 'post'" -> ask for `python -c 'import httpx; print(httpx.__file__)'` and `pip freeze`.

support-bot: Account check: customer (acme-corp) had no billing outages, token looked valid historically. No rate-limit issues. Not a platform auth regression.

olivia: timeline: customer back to green after non-editable install. Filing ENG ticket RED-8421 with repro and customer details, linking to this thread. Will update KB article and add playbook snippet.

carla: thanks — assign to eng-runtime for the import-detection patch, and to docs for a quick blurb. If someone wants, I can draft the KB. :thumbsup:

olivia: I'll follow up with the customer tomorrow to confirm no regressions and close the escalation.

mike: thx team.
